title: I was not familiar with either of these actors before seeing the show...
transcript: I've always been fascinated by stories about two people that are perfect for each other, but life and circumstances never quite line up for them to be together. Think movies like LA LA Land or once. Well, the play Shifters, which is now playing off Broadway, very much felt in that same vein to me. It is about two people who keep shifting in and out of each other's lives. And while their chemistry is undeniable, they are constantly pulled apart by circumstance and brought back together by fate. And I think this is a good time to shout out the two actors here, Heather Agyepong and Daniel Ezra, both of whom are giving fantastic performances, imbuing these characters with so much depth. And their chemistry together is electric. From the second that they are together on stage, you can feel that electricity, which means you are really rooting for them from the jump. But, of course, this isn't your typical romcom, and while I will not spoil if they do eventually end up together, their journey is certainly a rocky one. We begin the play with the two characters meeting in present day, having gone a long time without seeing each other. And throughout this encounter, we are constantly flashing backwards to previous interactions, eventually getting a pretty full scope of their entire relationship. The story is told non linearly, which makes it a little bit hard to follow at times. And clocking in at an hour and 45 Minutes, no intermission, It is probably a little bit longer than it needs to be. but it is undeniably a really compelling portrait of two very complicated people, and with two incredibly strong lead performances to keep you engaged from start to finish. Shifters is definitely going to be a Broadway Ben recommendation.
reasoning: Clear recommendation with praise for performances and chemistry, but notable caveats about non-linear storytelling being hard to follow and runtime feeling too long.
keyQuote: Shifters is definitely going to be a Broadway Ben recommendation.
